slides.title: ICMP Type
slides.body:
Time Exceeded
Code 0 - TTL exceeded in transit: Router decremented TTL to 0 and discarded the packet
Code 1 - Fragment reassembly time exceeded: Destination was waiting for all fragments to arrive, but they did not arrive in time. It discards all received fragments and reports the error

slides.title: Traceroute
slides.body:
Introduction
Ping tells you if a destination is reachable. Traceroute tells you exactly which routers a packet passes through - and how long each hop takes

slides.title: Traceroute
slides.body:
Introduction
The Core Idea: Exploit TTL deliberately
TTL starts at a value (typically 1, 2, 3, ...) and a router decrements it. When TTL = 0, the router discards the packet and sends back an ICMP Time Exceeded (Type 11, Code 0) - and crucially, that ICMP message comes from the router's own IP address

slides.title: Traceroute
slides.body:
How Traceroute Works (Step-by-Step)
Send a probe packet with TTL = 1 → first router discards it and replies with ICMP Time Exceeded → Hop 1 identified
Send with TTL = 2 → reaches second router → it replies → Hop 2 identified
Continue increasing TTL (3, 4, 5...) → each router reveals itself when TTL expires

slides.title: Traceroute
slides.body:
How Traceroute Works (Step-by-Step)
When the packet reaches the destination, it sends:
ICMP Echo Reply (Windows) or
ICMP Port Unreachable (Linux/UDP) → route complete

slides.title: Traceroute
slides.body:
Why 3 probes per hop?
Traceroute sends 3 probe packets per TTL value to give a statistical RTT reading - accounting for temporary fluctuations. The three RTT values shown are from those 3 probes

slides.title: Traceroute
slides.body:
The * * * case
When you see * * *, it means the router at that hop did not send an ICMP reply. This could be because: 
the router is configured to not reply to ICMP probes (firewall/policy), or 
the router replies were lost. However, the path beyond that hop can still succeed - * * * does not mean the path is broken

slides.title: Traceroute vs Tracert
slides.body:
Two Implementations, Same TTL Trick
The underlying concept of traceroute is identical on all platforms - deliberately expire TTL and collect ICMP Time Exceeded responses. The difference is in what probe packet they send
